notes: Large-source-unit check: שִׁיתוּ לִבְּכֶם לְ → 'Mark ye well'. Accounted morpheme by morpheme: 'Mark' carries the whole idiom (set heart to), 'well' its emphasis, and no English word answers to שִׁית, לֵב or לְ alone; the 2mp suffix's referent is carried by the same 'ye' that marks the imperative's subject, so the four-morpheme noncompositional unit is retained. The competing partition (suffix unrepresented outside the idiom) is defensible but not clearly preferable under rule 2.
